**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 21.1 cap quantum.**

Section 21 is well-built in most respects: the cap is expressly mutual, 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully treats data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response as direct damages), 21.3 carries the full preferred carve-out set as "Excluded Claims", and Customer's payment obligation is excluded from "damages".

The defect is the cap base. The cap runs to "the **Fees** paid or payable by Customer under the **first Order Form**", and §1.5 defines "Fees" as only the "Implementation Fee" — a one-time USD 12,000 charge (§1.6). Recurring subscription and service charges fall outside the cap entirely, so the mutual cap is effectively ~USD 12,000: well below the fallback of 12 months' fees and into walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees).

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) makes the smallest possible change — only the cap base in 21.1 — to the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding 12 months and (b) USD 1,000,000. Carve-outs left untouched.

Noted but not flagged here: §7.7's 15%-per-week liquidated damages on late invoices is a separate commercial issue for the payment/remedies rule.
